baselines: A naive submission with empty or incorrect register names and cycle index must fail all metrics.

metrics.description: Proportion of correctly identified vulnerable registers and cycles out of the total ground truth set.
metrics.name: leakage_detection_accuracy

metrics.description: Whether the reported vulnerability covers the critical fault injection point that leads to unauthorized access.
metrics.name: fault_coverage

metrics.description: Precision of the hardening suggestions derived from the vulnerability report, measured as the ratio of correct suggestions to total suggestions.
metrics.name: hardening_precision

acceptance_criteria: vulnerable_cycle equals the ground truth cycle index.
hidden_spec.ground_truth: Skipping auth_result_q while state_q advances at the compare-to-decide boundary leaves a stale pass value; redundant state/result encoding or fail-closed transition coupling blocks it.

security_requirements.detection_strategy: Check if vulnerable_cycle matches the ground truth cycle index derived from the normal trace and fault model.
security_requirements.requirement: The report must correctly identify the vulnerable cycle as the cycle where the state transitions from COMPARE to DECIDE.

security_requirements.detection_strategy: Check if state_register and result_register match the exact signal names in the ground truth.
security_requirements.requirement: The report must correctly identify the state register as state_q and the result register as auth_result_q.

hidden_spec.threat_model: An attacker injects a narrow clock glitch during authentication and causes inconsistent updates that grant access without a valid comparison.

constraints: The analysis must be based solely on the provided input artifacts.
The fault model describes a single clock cycle where one register update is skipped while combinational logic continues to evaluate.
The normal trace represents the expected cycle-by-cycle behavior without faults.
expected_outputs: A vulnerability_report.json file identifying the vulnerable cycle and the critical state/result signals.

functional_requirements.requirement: The submitted vulnerability_report.json must be valid JSON and parseable by a standard JSON parser.
The report must identify exactly one vulnerable_cycle as an integer.
The report must name a state_register and a result_register that exist as signal names in the provided auth_fsm.v file.
The explanation field must be a non-empty string describing the vulnerability mechanism.

public_spec.interface: The participant submits a single JSON file at submission/vulnerability_report.json. The file must contain an object with the following keys: "vulnerable_cycle" (integer, the clock cycle index where the fault is injected), "state_register" (string, the exact signal name of the state register in the RTL), "result_register" (string, the exact signal name of the result register in the RTL), and "explanation" (string, a brief description of the vulnerability mechanism).
public_spec.objective: Analyze the provided RTL design and fault model to locate the state and result registers where one skipped update can move an authentication controller from compare directly to grant.
public_spec.response_format: A JSON object with keys: vulnerable_cycle (integer), state_register (string), result_register (string), explanation (string).

title: Clock-glitch window in authentication state transition
